last.verdict: Opendoor bought far more homes than it sold, and profit per home sold fell, so the loss widened to $218M and the debt load grew.

takeaways.label: Margins fell sharply
takeaways.text: Profit per home sold fell: contribution margin was 3.3% versus 5.8% last quarter, and gross margin was 3.7% versus 9.7%. Writedowns on unsold homes rose to $53M from $14M.

takeaways.label: Inventory and debt ballooned
takeaways.text: Opendoor bought 4,865 homes but sold 2,728. Inventory reached $2.57B (7,596 homes), funded mostly by borrowing. Asset-backed debt is about $2.36B, and most of it is due within a year.

takeaways.label: Growth missed its target
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 12% to $1.02B, short of the 'at least 20%' growth the company guided to in August. Net loss widened to $218M from $90M a year ago.

takeaways.label: Tough Q4 outlook
takeaways.text: Opendoor expects Q4 revenue up at least 40% year over year, but profit dollars to fall and an adjusted EBITDA loss of $70M–$85M. It says it is 'selling into a difficult market'.

history.verdict: Investors sold on a weak margin outlook despite revenue and cash-burn improvement.

reasons.label: Lower margin outlook
reasons.text: Next-quarter contribution margin guided to 4%–4.5%, below this quarter's 5.8%, blamed on seasonality.

reasons.label: Sales far below last year
reasons.text: Revenue was $883M, down about 44% from a year ago, and below analyst estimates.

reasons.label: Bigger loss, mostly stock pay
reasons.text: Net loss was $162M versus $29M a year ago, driven by about $119M of stock-based pay.
